security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown documentation false positives, including code fences, inline backticks, placeholder URLs, and azd-managed paths. Confirmed risks remain for the predictable temp file hook, environment value disclosure, and RBAC role assignments that require explicit review before execution.

remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp with cleanup, quote paths, and store transient files under an environment-specific workspace directory.
Guard azd env get-values usage and require redaction before sharing command output in chat, logs, or tickets.
Require explicit user approval, document exact resource scopes, and apply least-privilege roles for each assignment.

semantic_findings.title: Environment Variable Disclosure Command
semantic_findings.description: The common command list includes azd env get-values to show all environment variables, while the skill also says azd env set is used for secrets. Running or sharing this output can expose secret values in transcripts or logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly labels azd env get-values as showing all env vars and separately identifies azd env set as the secret handling path. This creates a clear disclosure risk if command output is copied into chat or logs.

semantic_findings.title: RBAC Role Assignment Hook
semantic_findings.description: The post-provision hook creates Azure role assignments for a service principal against Azure OpenAI and Search scopes. This can grant cloud resource access if run without explicit scope review and approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The YAML hook directly runs az role assignment create with service principal assignees and resource scopes. The commands are legitimate but high impact in a deployment workflow.

content.user_title: Deploy Apps to Azure Container Apps
content.value_statement: Azure Container Apps deployments need consistent project files, environment variables, and identity setup. This skill guides azd, Bicep, remote builds, and RBAC patterns for repeatable deployments.
actual_capabilities: Maps azure.yaml options for frontend and backend Container Apps services.
Shows azd environment commands for creating, selecting, and setting environments.
Explains Bicep parameter injection from azd environment variables.
Provides managed identity and Azure RBAC hook patterns.
Documents remote Docker builds and Container Apps service discovery.
Lists common azd deployment and debugging commands.
limitations: Does not create or validate Azure resources by itself.
Requires Azure Developer CLI, Azure CLI, and subscription permissions.
Examples must be adapted before use in production environments.
May expose secrets if environment values are printed in logs.

use_cases.title: Standardize Container App Deployments
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable azd and Bicep structure for frontend and backend services.

use_cases.title: Deploy Full-Stack Applications
use_cases.description: Plan remote builds, service definitions, and environment variables for a containerized app.

use_cases.title: Review Identity and Access Patterns
use_cases.description: Check managed identity outputs and RBAC assignment hooks before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a First Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline the azd files and commands needed to deploy my frontend and backend to Azure Container Apps.

prompt_templates.title: Map Environment Variables
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to map my app settings into azd environment variables and Bicep parameters. Call out any secret handling risks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Deployment Hooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my azure.yaml hooks for custom domains, managed identity, and RBAC. Suggest safer changes before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a production deployment plan with remote builds, service discovery, managed identity, RBAC scopes, and rollback checks.

output_examples.input: I need to deploy a React frontend and Python backend to Azure Container Apps.
output_examples.output: Recommended structure includes azure.yaml, infra Bicep modules, service Dockerfiles, azd environment setup, and remote build settings.

output_examples.input: Review my deployment plan before I run azd up.
output: Checks environment selection and active subscription.
Reviews RBAC scopes and managed identity outputs.
Flags secret handling and commands that need approval.

output_examples.input: I need managed identity access to Azure OpenAI.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines a post-provision RBAC pattern and reminds you to scope roles to the smallest required resource.

best_practices: Confirm subscription, environment name, and target resource group before provisioning.
Use managed identity and least-privilege RBAC instead of embedded credentials.
Review hook commands and secret output before running them.
anti_patterns: Running deployment commands without confirming the active Azure subscription.
Printing azd environment values that may contain secrets.
Copying sample hooks into production without replacing placeholder names and scopes.

faq.question: What does this skill help deploy?
faq.answer: It helps plan azd deployments for frontend and backend services on Azure Container Apps.

faq.question: Does it run Azure commands automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide command execution, but deployment commands should require explicit user confirmation.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: Azure Developer CLI, Azure CLI, Docker files, Bicep infrastructure, and Azure subscription permissions are required.

faq.question: Can it handle secrets?
faq.answer: It explains azd environment variables, but secret values should not be printed or stored in prompt transcripts.

faq.question: Does it support managed identity?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for system-assigned identity and role assignments.

faq.question: Is it safe for production?
faq.answer: Use it as a checklist. Review scopes, hooks, costs, and environment settings before production deployment.
